req.title: Redirect preserves relative or absolute style
req.statement: The system shall emit relative URLs on /redirect/<n> and absolute URLs on /absolute-redirect/<n>.
triggers: redirect preserves relative or absolute style

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that GET /redirect/<n> emits relative URLs (no scheme/host) and GET /absolute-redirect/<n> emits absolute URLs (with scheme+host). The source code for redirect_n_times shows: when ?absolute=false (default), it calls _redirect('relative', n, False) or redirect(url_for('view_get', _external=False)); when ?absolute=true, it calls _redirect('absolute', n, True) or redirect(url_for('view_get', _external=True)). Tests must verify: (1) relative Location header on /redirect/<n> without ?absolute=true, (2) absolute Location header on /redirect/<n>?absolute=true, (3) boundary n=1 relative, (4) boundary n=1 absolute, (5) n=2 relative chain, (6) invalid n=0 (assert n>0 triggers 500/AssertionError), (7) exact Location header format. Mutation resilience: assert exact status codes (302 not >=300), assert Location header starts with '/' for relative and 'http' for absolute, assert exact n=1 boundary behavior.

tests.name: test_redirect_relative_n1_location_is_relative
preconditions: n=1 is the minimum valid redirect count
expected: Location header starts with '/' (relative URL, no scheme or host)
trace: R-HTTPBIN-042: relative URL on /redirect/<n>
source line: redirect(url_for('view_get', _external=False)) when n==1 and absolute==False
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_relative_n1_location_is_relative():
    r = client.get('/redirect/1', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 302
    location = r.headers['Location']
    assert location.startswith('/'), f'Expected relative URL starting with /, got: {location}'
    assert not location.startswith('http://'), f'Expected relative URL, got absolute: {location}'
    assert not location.startswith('https://'), f'Expected relative URL, got absolute: {location}'
    assert '/get' in location

test_redirect_relative_n1_location_is_relative()

tests.name: test_redirect_n2_relative_chain_second_hop
preconditions: n=2 relative: first hop goes to /redirect/1, second to /get
trace: R-HTTPBIN-042 BVA: n=2 boundary tests chaining logic
catches n-1 vs n mutation in _redirect
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_n2_relative_chain_second_hop():
    r1 = client.get('/redirect/2', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r1.status_code == 302
    loc1 = r1.headers['Location']
    assert loc1.startswith('/'), f'First hop must be relative, got: {loc1}'
    assert 'redirect' in loc1, f'n=2 first hop should point to another redirect, got: {loc1}'
    r2 = client.get(loc1, follow_redirects=False)
    assert r2.status_code == 302
    loc2 = r2.headers['Location']
    assert loc2 == '/get', f'Second hop (n=1) must go to /get, got: {loc2}'
    r3 = client.get(loc2)
    assert r3.status_code == 200

test_redirect_n2_relative_chain_second_hop()
